title: Office Plant Care and Desk Jungle Guidelines
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This page documents lightweight, community-driven guidelines for caring for office plants and maintaining a pleasant desk-plant ecosystem. It is intended to keep shared spaces tidy, reduce plant mortality, and provide simple escalation paths for issues. These guidelines are informal and may be superseded by facility vendor contracts or building policies.

Scope:
- Applies to all plants in shared spaces (kitchen, conference rooms, lounge) and to potted plants kept at individual desks when they interact with shared facilities (water stations, plant shelves).
- Excludes customer office gardens and third-party contracted plant maintenance.

Principles:
1. Low-effort, resilient plants preferred: choose hardier species for communal areas (e.g., pothos, snake plant, ZZ plant).
2. Shared responsibility: facilities owns ordering and large maintenance; community volunteers do day-to-day checks.
3. Non-judgmental culture: if a plant is wilting, flag it; no shaming.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Facilities (Facilities Manager): owns budget, vendor coordination, pest escalation, and the monthly supplies reorder.
- Desk Jungle Stewards (rotating volunteers): 1-2 people per floor who perform weekly checks and watering for shared-planter zones.
- Individual Employees: responsible for personal desk plants (follow desk guidelines below).

Weekly Care Schedule (recommended):
1. Monday: Steward inspects shared planters, notes soil moisture, and rotates plants if shade distribution is uneven.
2. Wednesday: Quick misting for humidity-sensitive plants (only in winter months).
3. Friday: Tidy loose soil, remove dead leaves, and record any pest signs in the shared Plant Log (Google Sheet link in related pages).

Desk Jungle Guidelines (for personal plants):
- Pot size: keep to 4–8 inch pots for desks; larger pots belong in floor planters.
- Watering: use a tray to prevent accidental spills; water at desk only in non-sensitive equipment areas.
- Lighting: if a plant requires bright light, place near windows; avoid blocking walkways.
- Allergies: pick hypoallergenic species when possible or keep plants contained inside cubicle boundaries.

Shared Planters & Conference Rooms:
- Labeling: all shared planter pots should have a small waterproof label with plant name and last-watering date.
- Rotation: every three months facilities will rotate plants to refresh displays and prevent one area bearing all sun/heat exposure.

Supplies & Ordering:
- Facilities will maintain a basic kit: peat-free potting mix, small pruning shears, plant food (low-dose), trays, and labels.
- To request supplies: submit a ticket in #facilities-requests Slack channel or file a help ticket (link in related pages). For emergency replacement (pests, floods), contact Facilities Manager directly.

Pests & Health Issues:
- Immediate action: isolate affected plant, take photos, and post to the Plant Log with time/date and steward name.
- Quarantine window: keep suspected plants isolated for 7–10 days; do not compost onsite without Facilities approval.
- Escalation: if pests persist or spread to multiple planters, Facilities will engage vendor or building management for treatment.

Event Use & Decorations:
- Temporary decorations (e.g., pot toppers, small plaques) allowed but must be removed within 48 hours after the event. No open flames or food-based decorations in shared planters.

Conflict Resolution:
- If a plant in a shared zone is being mistreated or over-cared (e.g., overwatered), leave a polite note on the shared Plant Log. If unresolved after one week, escalate to the Facilities Manager who will mediate.

FAQ:
- Q: Can I rehome my unhealthy desk plant into a shared planter?
  A: No — rehoming must be approved by a Steward after assessment to avoid introducing pests or disease.
- Q: Who pays for a replacement plant I broke?
  A: Personal desk plants are the owner’s responsibility; accidental damage to shared planters should be reported and may be covered by the facilities petty fund depending on circumstances.

Appendix (quick reference table):
Plant Type | Best Location | Water Frequency | Notes
Pothos | Low light zones, shelves | Every 10–14 days | Very tolerant of neglect
Snake Plant | Desks with very low light | Every 3–6 weeks | Avoid overwatering
Rubber Plant | Bright indirect light | Every 7–10 days | Trim to control size
